2003.label: Pre-Season
2003.text:
Ladies and gentlemen... (I say ladies only based on the way some of you drafted, your wives or girlfriends had to be in the war room with you)  Welcome to the MFFL 2003 Edition.

I am Marc Muchnick, your league Commissioner.  Each week I hope to provide you with my commentary on the week's events, who shined, who stinks, and most of all how I thought each GM handled their team.  Of course, with the birth of my first child only days away, that could and may well be completely thrown out the window.  That said, let me say how excited I am about the upcoming football season and most of all the MFFL.  Thanks to everyone who has paid me already (note: that does not include John Stafford or Marty Hansen!).

League expansion is done, the rule changes are locked in, the draft is over, now on to the analysis.  I thought I would start out by doing a brief analysis of each teams strengths and weaknesses as I see them and conclude the pre-season with our first MFFL Power Rankings. 

Wildcats II - (Owner: Scott Zide)

Scott made a huge run in the playoffs last year finishing in 2nd after finishing in 7th or 8th place during the regular season barely sneaking into the playoffs.  He was led most of the way by his QB, Rich Gannon and his 40-50 point weeks.  This year Scott decided to use his 8th pick overall to go after running backs and waited until the 4th round to pick up Gannon's replacement in Trent Green.  Green put up huge numbers last year (on Chris's bench) and should do the same again this year as long as Priest Holmes can keep the focus on him and not the passing game.  The Wildcats roster doesn't really have any stars, in that I mean top 5 players at their position.  However it is fairly deep at Wide Receiver with a lot of quality guys like Holt, Hilliard, Brown and Bradford.  While each of these guys have the talent, they all struggled to get in the end zone last year.  Scott's best picks of the draft were Atlanta's D in the 8th and J.J. Stokes in the 13th round.  Overall, balanced but middle of the pack like his draft position.

Syracuse Orangemen - (Owner: Marty Hansen)

Marty struggled most of last year with the amount of time he could focus on the league.  He was unable to continually monitor the free agent and waiver wire and missed out on several key pickups that could have helped his team into the playoffs.  This year, Marty looks to benefit from the reduction in bench depth and hopes it will balance the league out and offer more options in the free agent market.  Marty had a good draft in my opinion despite his 11th position which is too far down to get a top back, yet not close enough on the return in the 2nd round to steal a top player at a position like WR.  Despite that Marty was able to take a strong backfield in Edgerrin James and Jamal Lewis.  Edge looks to see a tremendous improvement this year and may be undervalued due to his injury history.  If he returns to form of three years ago, Marty may have the steal of the 1st round, just like John Stafford's selections of Priest Holmes and Ricky Williams with the 12th and 13th picks last year.  Marty is weak at QB while he waits for Mike Vick to return and has to rely on Mark Brunell.  He snagged a solid TE core in Gonzales and McMichael although I believe it was too early in the draft and depth at TE is one of those things we can't afford with a 5 man bench.  Overall Marty puts a strong team on the field although age could be a problem this year.  His WR core and is suspect with Bruce, Rice and McCardell who all may be beyond their prime.  Not one #1 receiver in the bunch.

Bubb Rubb Allstars - (Owner: Loren Muchnick)

No one in the league is quite as excited for the year to start as Loren.  He had a solid team last year and if I remember correctly lost out in the early rounds of the playoffs.  Loren looked at his 14th pick in the draft as a positive being able to take back to back picks and having 2 selections in the top 15.  No one else could say that.  He stuck to his game plan and loaded up at RB with his top 2 selections.  Barber earned huge numbers for me last year with his ability to put up 100 yards and catch at least 4-5 balls a game.  Loren has already been active in the free agent market picking up Robert Ferguson and Olandis Gary who each should get a lot of playing time this year.  In addition, Loren looks to take advantage of his #1 waiver position and swoop in on the first bye week casualty.  Although it may come for Loren in the 4th week of the season before anyone else has to drop star players.  The Bubb Rubb Allstars have decent depth at WR and RB and a pretty solid QB in Aaron Brooks.  Although I believe its in the free agent market where Loren will overcome his draft position and make a run this year.  As soon as an unknown player breaks 100 yards during the week, you better get online to snag him because I guarantee Loren will have his HTPC ready to go.

Chasin the Boilers - (Owner: Doug Evernham)

Doug used his high pick well and was able to snag 3 quality players in the early rounds of the draft in Holmes, Gannon, and Boston.  Beyond that it gets a little shaky with some of Doug's selections, most notably Bubba Franks in the 5th round.  Franks wasn't even the top TE on the board not to mention that he probably could have got him in the 7th round.  Franks looks to share his TD production with Wesley Walls this year and could see a large dropoff in his numbers.  In addition, selections like Tim Brown and Tyrone Wheatley.  Brown struggled to do well last year as the #2 receiver in Oakland and this year has moved down the depth chart behind Jerry Porter.  Wheatley may not even be the 4th best back in Oakland behind Garner, Crockett and possibly Justin Fargas.  Overall, Doug has three star players which could possibly carry him this year.  If John Stafford would have had Gannon to go with Holmes last year, he would have been league champ for sure.  Lets just hope the duo can repeat their effort this year.

Palmer MVP - (Owner: Rae Buck)

Rae finished in 4th place last year losing the 3-4 game to me and had to pay up on our case of beer side bet.  Rae can only hope to do that well this year.  Unfortunately for Rae, he will play this season under the curse of the Catholic School Girls.  You see Rae had to miss the draft to attend an orientation at his girl's new school.  His pre-rankings didn't hold up well and Rae was stuck with players like Jimmy Smith, Chad Pennington and Jerome Bettis.   None of which will see any playing time in the near future.  If Rae can survive the early part of the season he may be able to rebound, but thats going to be tough.  He'll need huge performances from his #1 overall selection, Ricky Williams.  While not always seen as the #1 overall player, he is still solid and should bring in huge numbers.  Rae's #2 pick in Jeff Garcia is a bit questionable as well.  While I believe he is a good player, he isn't worth the 28th pick and 3rd overall QB taken.  An injury prone preseason put him as far down as the 7th-10th round in most leagues.  Rae's best pickup may have been Hines Ward in the 3rd round.  Ward earned Loren huge unexpected points last year and should do well with Maddox at the helm in Pittsburgh this year.  Overall, a couple of stars, but very little depth and not the kind of team you would expect with the #1 overall pick.

The Balance Cheats - (Owner: Ed Muchnick)

Ed came into the draft with what some would call the ideal draft position, 7th overall, which gives him one pick in every 14 selections.  With a top 7 player and the ability to get in on the runs on key positions, Ed came in looking good.  After the draft, Ed ended up a a pretty strong team with stars at almost every key position including defense.  The only weak spots are at Tight End, his #2 back and a little too much emphasis on the Rams.  Ed snagged a top back in McCallister, a top QB in McNabb, the top overall defense, and solid depth at WR with Coles and Mason.  I expect Ed will need to hit the free agency wire in about two weeks once he realizes Cam Cleeland isn't the player he used to be.  If you find yourself lacking in QB towards week 8 or 9, Ed's your guy with McNabb, Brad Johnson and Marc Bulger.  It remains to be seen if he can afford to hold three QBs and whether Warner will falter like everyone expects.

Super Chargers - (Owner: Todd Yates)

Todd enters the league this year as one of two expansion teams.  While he may lack the experience with our scoring system, his draft doesn't show it.  His top three picks of Ahman Green, Moulds and Bledsoe are strong although they do rely on the success of the Bills offense.  Without Price, Moulds may get too much attention limiting his numbers.  Bledsoe certainly is a solid pick given that he likes to throw 30-40 times in a game.  Yates, unfortunately is the first GM to suffer a major post-draft setback losing James Stewart for the season and not having a chance to take Gary as his replacement.  The Super Chargers have plenty of depth at WR with Stallworth, Moss, Andre Johnson, Dez White and Muhammad to back up Moulds, however this leaves them a little weak at RB forcing Todd to start Marcel Shipp.  Philadelphia's D should be good for about 10 points a week.  TE may be a little soft with the emergence of Dallas Clark taking catches from Pollard in Indy.  Overall, strong team, only a couple of holes, worth paying attention to.

Cincinnati Hustler - (Owner: Marc Muchnick, The Commish)

This is the greatest team I have ever seen assembled!!!  Just kidding, I'll try and be as objective as possible about my own roster.  After a 3rd place finish last year, and my only playoff loss to the eventual champion Chris, Hustler look to rebound.   Another year without a top 5 or even top 10 back could be the demise of my team.   I was frustrated to see the run on RBs before me in the draft, I honestly thought I might snag Shawn Alexander or worse case Edge with my pick.  Not even close, Fred Taylor is a huge gamble with a #1 pick although I expect bigger things from him now that Stacey Mack isn't there to steal his TDs.  Zereuoe is a question mark and so is Mack for that matter given that Texas rarely gets to the red zone.  QB is solid, although Favre has definitely lost a step.  I can only hope Moss returns to becoming a top 3 back as far as production goes.  Beyond that Travis Taylor, Curtis Conway, and Ashley Lelie are all risks.   Overall, a top 3 WR, a top 5-10 QB, a top 3 TE, and a top 5 defense.  Lots of gambles which if they pay off will reap huge reward come playoff time, if not another huge flop with the 13th overall draft position.

Wildwood Old School - (Owner: Chris Baumgartner)

Chris is back this year looking for a repeat to his MFFL title and will be targeted as much as the Tampa Bay Bucs. GMs like Steve Briscoe and myself will be looking to prove that his run from 8th to 1st in the playoffs was a fluke.  That may not be easy with the balance his roster brings this year.  Chris suprised many people by gambling a bit on Marshall Faulk with the #2 pick instead of taking Tomlinson which most league's had ranked as the #1 overall player.  He also stuck to his game plan better than most by not falling victim to the QB run in the middle rounds.  Chris instead built a solid RB core and a young but talented WR core to shape his team around.  Middle of the road QBs like Collins and McNair were available in the later rounds and both can put up the numbers Chris will need to get over the top each week.   I really like Koren Robinson and Chad Johnson, although I think it drops off from there with Derrius Thompson and Todd Pinkston.  Overall, great balance, great shot at the title again.

Top Shelf - (owner: John Briscoe)

John returns to the MFFL looking to learn from his mistakes last year.  A year more experience and hopes that injuries won't plague him like they did last year with his top 2 picks, Faulk and James.  John also stuck to his draft plan and loaded up on WR while waiting on his QB to the later rounds.  In return, he got his man in Maddox and built by far the league's top WR core with Harrison, Driver and Price.  Not to mention, Reggie Wayne and Steve Smith on the bench.  John's big weakness is definitely going to be at running back with two aging stars in Martin and Hearst.  Both have been known to lose the goal line carries.  Martin espects to get more carries with Pennington out, however defenses should be keying on him more as well.  I like Jolley at TE, however I think New England's D was a bit of a reach with Miami and Philadelphia still on the board.  Overall, this is going to be a great team if his RBs can come through for 15-20 points a week.

Steelers 03 - (Owner: John Stafford)

John was near the top of the leaderboard almost every week last season, mainly due to his solid RB core of Holmes and Williams.  The only reason we didn't see John in the championship game was due to Holmes injury and his lack of depth at QB.  The 03 edition of the Steelers looks to take it a step further in the playoffs by adding more depth at QB and a little more balance.  John got a great player in Portis with his 1st pick, but by the time his 2nd pick came around there wasn't much in the way of RBs available.  Warner is definitely a risk, but if he comes through and puts up 40+ points a week again, this is going to be a solid team.  Not to mention the fact that John has Hasselbeck, a very underrated QB, on the bench.  I passed up on him for Favre and I know I'm going to regret it at some point this season.  With a top QB on the bench, John may have enough for trade to improve his #2 RB position.  WRs are good, not great, Burress looks to be a top 5 WR with Maddox starting.  Carolina D is another that I am going to regret passing on, but I have a feeling John would be willing to trade for the Steelers D at anytime.  

End Zone Gang - (Owner: Steve Briscoe)

Steve was the league champion last year, well sort of, if you don't count the playoffs he was.   But then again whats the point in winning if you can't win in the playoffs.  Kind of like Peyton Manning and the Colts.  Or the Dolphins for that matter, right Steve?  This year, Steve had to trade in Marvin Harrison for Terrell Owens as his son, John, stole him with the pick before him.  Two completely different players as far as point production, one is consistant, the other gets huge spurts that can win games for you.  Steve's biggest weakness is going to be his reliance on the 49ers offense, he has 3 starters on their team in Owens, Streets and Barlow.  I love Tai Streets and expect him to have a great year and be the guy to balance out Owens spurts.  However, if Garcia continues to have back problems and hte Niners are shut out one week, its going to be tough to win for Steve.  Brady and Dillon are great picks in my opinion.  I expect both to put up more TDs this year, Brady is always good with his high completion percentage and number of attempts.  In addition, Steve's ace in the hole is 10-12 points a week from Shockey at TE, a position most don't expect to get much out of this year.  Again, another top team to watch out for, RB could be a little too thin.

4th and Inches - (Owner: Andrew Briscoe)

Andrew too may carry a curse on his team this year.  Along with Rae, Andrew gave us nice 90 second breaks during the draft because he decided to bail after three rounds due to a nagging hangover from partying the night before.  I realize my priorities are out of whack being the old man I am, but I thought it was fantasy football that led TO the drinking, not drinking that leads you AWAY from fantasy football.  Regardless, Andrew lucked out a bit and still managed a decent team.  His top three picks are great in Alexander, Manning and Horn.  I thought Horn went a little too soon, but he is a guy that I remember always burning me in head to heads last year.  Manning was a steal in the 3rd round given that I burned a 1st round pick on him last year.  Andrew has depth at WR, RB, a solid up and coming TE, and a good D.  Thanks Yahoo!

Tenacious D - (Owner: Steve King)

Last but definitely not least, Steve King, the leagues other expansion GM rounds out the 14 team MFFL this year.  Steve is the only person I know of who followed my weekly posts and scouted other GMs last year even though he wasn't in the league.  Thats more than a lot of GMs in the league did.  Steve is notorious for being the most educated and up to date on the ongoings in the NFL.  He studies fantasy football more than anyone, we shall see if it pays off for him in December this year.  So far, so good, although I simply scouted the teams in order of listing on the pre-season standings, I believe I saved the best team for last.  Steve doesn't have any real weaknesses in his roster.  He has a top 5 QB, 3 solid WRs in my opinion, the #1 overall back, and a great #2 in Stephen Davis.  I suppose if I were to nitpick, his weaknesses would be TE and the Rams D, but who cares, those are secondary positions for most.  There is always a great TE and a under appreciated D on the free agent wire.  He even has good backups in Josh Reed and Duce Staley who eventually will become the undisputed #1 back again in Philly.  If his team is as good as I think it is, we may need to contract the league next year and go back to 12 teams.

So, 14 teams, a mild case of carpel-tunnel syndrome, and a lot of optimism for the coming year.  Before I leave, here are the pre-season MFFL POWER RANKINGS:

1) Tenacious D
2) Wildwood Old School
3) 4th and Inches
4) End Zone Gang
5) Top Shelf
6) Steelers 03
7) Cincinnati Hustler
8) Chasin the Boilers
9) The Balance Cheats
10) Super Chargers
11) Wildcats II
12) Syracuse Orangemen
13) Bubb Rubb Allstars
14) Palmer MVP

Remember, tonight is opening night, be sure to get your rosters set.  Good luck to everyone and thanks again for being a part of my league.  Can't wait to get it underway.

Until next time,

THE COMMISH  

NOTE: The comments and views of Marc Muchnick DO necessarily represent those of this league and its management.  Don't like em', thats why they play the game.

2003.label: Week 1
2003.text:
One week down, 15 more to go before the MFFL is decided.  Week 1 featured some teams with a suprise burst of offense that I didn't think they had in them, namely the 14th ranked (according to me) Palmer MVP.  There was some scoring contreversy, lots of new injuries, and overall more parity than the 2002 edition of the MFFL.  The top score was 103.18 by Doug Evernham's Chasin the Boilers.  Last season we regularly saw scores in the 120s and 130s.  In addition, we witnessed what I believe to be the worst week of MFFL Fantasy Football in our short 2 year history by Steve Briscoe and the (Can't find the) End Zone Gang.  39.51 points total.  Loren's son Tyler (21 months old) could have picked a roster out of a hat that put up more points than that. :)  Sorry Steve, hate to kick you when you are down, especially after your Dolphins lost to the Texans and your Boilermakers lost to Bowling Green at home.  Not to mention the Cardinals dropping out of the Central division race.  Do me a favor, can you root for the 49ers this week, the Rams need a win.

On to the recaps:

Chasin the Boilers (1-0) v. Palmer MVP (0-1)

The game of the week this week, decided in the final minutes of the Sunday night game.  At first it appeared this game was decided by Gannon downing the ball to stop the clock with 7 seconds to go.  However, after some scoring corrections, Doug was able to overcome Rae by a 6 point margin.  Doug got the last laugh on myself and everyone else who decided to pass on last year's top producers, Priest Holmes and Rich Gannon.  Priest earned more points than the top 3 picks combined (Williams, Tomlinson and Faulk).  Gannon wasn't stellar but again completed the majority of his 38 attempts for over 250 yards and 2 TDs.  Contrary to my belief, Tim Brown even put up decent numbers with a TD in the 2nd half of the Raiders game.  I thought I was going to be right after his 0 catches at halftime, but he came on strong and showed he still may have some value left in him.  Rae put up good numbers, but again fell just short.  One could say this matchup came down to Rae's lack of a 2nd RB.  Holding out hope that Bettis would end up with the redzone carries, Rae was left disappointed.  Bettis had a chance as he was put in in the 2nd quarter but he too couldn't muster anything against the Ravens D.  Rae's top 3 performed well, with Garcia leading the way, looks like the back is fine.  Although he did play the Bears.  Next week, Doug should get some more production from Franks with the lack of WRs in Green Bay.  Both teams face 1-0 teams next week.

Bubb Rubb All Stars (1-0) v. End Zone Gang (0-1)

The only person Loren needs to thank this week for his win is Kurt Warner.  His 4 fumble recoveries, 6 sacks and defensive TD led the All Stars to their first victory.  Beyond his defense, only Loren's kicker put up good numbers this week.  Brooks was off, not one of his WRs or RBs earned a TD, yet he still won by 52 points.  Good Luck with that next week against Gannon and Holmes.  For Steve, I've said enough about his team's performance.  Brady actually cost him points last week, a first I believe for a QB who played the entire game.   Steve's WRs actually did okay with some decent numbers, but Dillon and his lack of a #2 RB cost him with only 5.65 points combined.  Things don't get much better next week as Brady will have to face the Eagles D.   Hopefully an injury depleted DB core will help him get back on track.

4th and Inches (1-0) v. Wildcats II (0-1)

A solid performance by rookie Charles Rogers was the difference in this match up.  Head to head, these two matched up well.  Manning and Green each had mediocre days passing, Holt and Horn were both strong each getting in the end zone once.  Both #1 RBs did really well while both #2 struggled.  Scott could have really used a few field goals from Vinatieri however Brady's redzone mistakes cost him.  Eddie George looks to be the same 2.1 YPG back he was last year, hopefully a few more goal line rushes will get Scott some points down the road.  Overall, no real suprises, next week the QBs production should both pick up. 

Syracuse Orangemen (1-0) v. Tenacious D (0-1)

My top seed has already fallen, it took Steve like 6 weeks last year before showing any signs of weakness.   Both teams came into this matchup with solid RB cores, however not one of the 4 saw the endzone this week.  For Steve, there is no way Tomlinson can continue to play the way he did in week 1.  For Marty, once Manning gets the Colts offense moving, Edge is sure to pick up his production as well.  I was a little suprised to see how little production Steve got from his WRs, especially from Jerry Porter who only earned .8 points this week.  Galloway, someone I've been coveting from day 1 was the only starter on Tenacious D who had a big game, excluding QBs.  Culpepper and Moss looked like they were back to their early days, trying to forget about last year which is a plus for both Steve and I.   Marty again made me look stupid this week by getting a huge game from Mark Brunell.  I never thought Brunell would be able to fill the void while Vick was out, but so far so good.  I think he only had like 4 incompletions all game.  Perhaps Jimmy Smith is better off on the bench.  Good call on dropping Kordell and going back to your 1st instinct on Brunell, Marty.

Tom Shelf (1-0) v. The Balance Cheats (0-1)

Ed had a decent chance of pulling a big comeback with his two top players going on Monday night (McNabb and Tampa D).  Unfortunately, one cancelled the other out.  Tampa was great, McNabb wasn't.  For John, his points came from some unlikely sources in Maddox and Hearst.  John's #1 rated WR core scored less than 10 points overall, and he lost Driver for an undetermined period of time.  Harrison will definitely pick it up, but not sure about Price in Atlanta.  Johnson struggled to find Peerless all game.  Not a good sign for John when Curtis Martin was pulled for Jordan in the redzone.  This could severely limit his production this year.  New England's D didn't hold up quite like John expected either, again only can get better from here.  For Ed, he finds himself in a good position in the coming weeks.  McNabb should improve, he has Bulger on the bench who should demand a good #2 RB, better than Amos Zeroeue apparently :).  Coles looked great in his Redskins debut and Mason was reliable as always.  Despite his loss, he should see a bump in the Power rankings with Bulger at the helm in STL.

Wildwood Old School (0-1) v. Super Chargers (1-0)

The rookie ended Chris's 4 or 5 game winning streak carrying over from last season.  Another close matchup, although not quite as much production here.  Chris went with Collins over McNair and it cost him as Collins struggled despite St. Louis's turnovers.  Outside of QB, Chris had a decent week, with Faulk being the only real exception.   Just goes to show you how valuable a good QB is in our league.   In Faulk's defense, he didn't get many carries, however he didn't look very good in the ones he did.  Blame Warner, blame the O-Line, we'll have to see next week if Bulger can open things up for Faulk and get Chris back to his winning ways.  For Yates, a wins a win.  His only really strong performance was from Ahman Green and his 2 TDs.  Bledsoe give most of the scoring to Travis Henry in week 1, although the double points he from Bledsoe to Moulds should pick up next week.  Just ask Steve B. what a huge lift this can be.  Major hole in the #2 RB position, maybe Bryson is a decent start, who knows.

Cincinnati Hustler (0-1) v. Steelers 03 (1-0)

And finally, the only game that was over by the time the 49ers kicked off in Chicago at 4:00pm EDT.  Both John and I had all our starters in 1:00pm games, and believe me its easier to lose right away then to scream at the TV on Monday Night when your Tight End can't catch the 3 balls you need to win.  Both of our QBs looked awful this week, although fortunate for me it looks like mine will rebound.  John knew Warner was a risk from day one, which is probably why he picked up Hasselback as insurance.  Portis led the way for John this week with 2 TDs and good yardage, tearing into the Bengals D.  Beyond that it came down to a few extra field goals and a stingy Carolina D.  I said it last week, I wasn't sure whether to take Carolina's D or Pittsburgh.  While I'm still okay with my choice, I would be 1-0 going into week 2 if I'd have changed my mind.  For me, I was happy to see Moss looked great, worth a #2 selection.  A gut reaction right before the games to go with Boerigter over Taylor cost me the win.  Looks like basing last years WR v. Team D matchups doesn't help much.  Lesson learned.  Taylor looked good, but struggled to score, Zereoue scored, but didn't look good.  Especially when Bettis came in for him in the 2nd quarter.  What the hell, Cowher!  Don't you realize we're playing Fantasy here?

So, there you have it, Week 1 in the books.  Lots of close match-ups should make this year a lot of fun.  Although as we saw in the Playoffs last year, it could mean an 8 seed can win it with a decent schedule in weeks 14-16.  Here are this week's Power Rankings:

1) 4th and Inches (1-0) - Solid week and still good depth.
2) Tenacious D (0-1) - Still a great roster, tough loss.
3) Top Shelf (1-0) - Big Suprise with Maddox, WRs should improve.
4) Wildwood Old School (0-1) A change in QB and he would #1 this week.
5) Steelers 03 (1-0) - Good solid win, depth keeps him high after injuries.
6) Chasin the Boilers (1-0) - Gannon and Holmes could take him to #1 in a couple weeks.
7) The Balance Cheats (0-1) - Depsite the loss, Bulger selection should make this team better.
8) Super Chargers (1-0) - Great lineup this week and a good win against the top seed.
9) Syracuse Orangemen (1-0) - Good win, lets see if Brunell can keep it up.
10) Cincinnati Hustler (0-1) - Will continue to fall until Favre can prove himself.
11) Bubb Rubb Allstars (1-0) - Easy win moves him up, but not too much yet.
12) Palmer MVP (0-1) - Near win moves him out of the cellar, Garcia could elevate this team further.
13) End Zone Gang  (0-1) - Huge loss = hugh fall in the rankings, still has a good lineup, can easily bounce back.
14) Wildcats II (0-1) - Still not a lot going for him.

Thanks all, no baby yet, keep your fingers crossed for me.  Talk to you all next week.

The Commish

2003.label: Week 2
2003.text:
Boy oh boy, what a week it was.  I can't remember a week in my life where I was so excited and so stressed out at the same time.  Monday night had to be the toughest though.  I stayed up half the night waiting for it to end.  I mean overtime between the Cowboys and Giants on MNF.  Jamal Lewis breaking the rushing record, the Rams pulling it out in overtime over the Niners, the Eagles and Titans at 0-2.   Wow, can it get any better than that?  Oh yeah, we had a baby this week too.  

Hehehe, I crack myself up sometimes.  Thanks to everyone who sent there best this week.  It was and has been like nothing I could ever have imagined.  But, enough about Katie, lets talk football.  Since I didn't have time to get the report out early in the week, I'm pulling together a condensed Saturday Night wrap-up of the week before.  

Week 2 again proved me wrong on my pre-season predictions, teams I thought were a fluke last week proved to have some legitate fire power.  Case and point, Palmer MVP, leading the league in points despite starting two players who see more bench than game.  Pick up a back RB Rae, come on!  We also came to realize that my team actually stinks.  I have 1 TD from all my RBs, WRs, and TE for the season.  However, I am not the worst in production, that distinction goes to Steve although his first week disaster is still dragging him down.  80 points in week 2 wasn't awful.  Bad call on starting Brees over Brady.  The Old School picked up their first win of the season behind a dominant Ravens defense.  Although to be fair, my team is so bad that both of my losses have been half=ass wins by my opponents.   But, a wins a win and thats all that matters.  Rae continues to put up points behind his top 3 Garcia, Ward, and Williams.  Alge Crumpler is turning out to be a steal making those of us who took Shockey, Gonzales and Heap look stupid.  John Stafford seems to have recovered from Warner's benching with a decent performance from Hasselbeck, although he isn't getting the number of attempts he achieved last season.  Plaxico Burress is still dominating, and Anquan Boldin may actually be a solid player after all.  

Todd Yates picked up his 2nd win of the season in impressive fashion knocking off his roommate John.   The Bledsoe to Moulds combination is working better for Yates than it did for Steve Briscoe last year.  John Briscoe did show me up with a 30 point effort from his New England D that I harped on the week before.  However, I'm not sure if they are going to last with the number of injuries they have.  Colvin for the year hurts.  Maddox so far is the smartest pick of the draft given how late he was taken.  John's only weakness has been his pathetic RB core which was suspected all along.  With Driver back in the lineup hopefully next week, John's WRs may be able to pick the slack back up.  My preseason favorite Tenacious D finally got in the win column and all it took was the dominant offense of the Vikings.  Dominant and Vikings, didn't think I'd say that this year.  Pass to Moss, Pass to Moss!!!  Ed's team is really underperforming so far.  Who'd have though McNabb would be the worst QB in the league?  Time to start Bulger dad.  No worries though, you still have Coles, McCallister and Tampa D.  

Marty again suprised me with his 2nd win and strong offensive numbers.  Brunell was okay, his WRs stunk, but when you have Jamal Lewis and Edge in the backfield, who needs WRs?  In addition, its nice to get 17 points from a kicker.  Unfortunately for Andrew it appears the number 1 seed in the power rankings is a bigger curse than the SI cover and the Madden cover.  Andrew was awful this week, only putting up 56 points.  What is going on with Peyton Manning?  Scott Zide was another one making me look bad, picking up his first win despite being last in the power rankings.  Two things are for sure, the top seed will lose and the bottom seed will win.  Guess where you are going to find the Cincinnati Hustler this week.  Scott was led by Travis Henry and his 4 TDs already this season.  However, looks like I was right about Eddie George, he is not a solid back anymore.  And finally, Loren continued to challenge me and my preseason 13th rank with his 2nd win.  Week 1 was a gimme, but week 2 was impressive.  Darrell Jackson picked up the slack for an injured Koren Robinson in Seattle, and Aaron Brooks outdid himself.  For Doug, Gannon showed his age against the Bengals D.  Not to mention Tim Brown's failure to product despite Porter being out of the lineup.  Priest is still dominant and should carry Doug just like he carried John Stafford last season.

So that does it for Week 2, bye weeks start this week and we should see some action on the free agent and waiver wire.  Matchups of the week are between Bubb Rubb and Palmer MVP, and the Tenacious D and Super Chargers.  Here are the power rankings:

1) Tenacious D (1-1)
2) Super Chargers (2-0) 
3) Syracuse Orangemen (2-0)
4) Wildwood Old School (1-1) 
5) Bubb Rubb Allstars (2-0)
6) Top Shelf (1-1)  
7) Steelers 03 (1-1)
8) 4th and Inches (1-1)
9) Palmer MVP (1-1)
10) Chasin the Boilers (1-1) 
11) The Balance Cheats (0-2) 
12) Wildcats II (1-1)
13) End Zone Gang (0-2)
14) Cincinnati Hustler (0-2)

Until next week, 

The Commish

2003.label: Week 3
2003.text:
What can I say other than the Commissioner's weekly wrap up is a vrey powerful tool in the MFFL.  It appears whatever team I say is bad, will surely win, whatever player I say is hot, will surely fail.  I commend Steve King for winning while ranked #1, if you call a 52 point effort by your competition a win of course.  Congrats to Marty Hansen as well for becoming the leagues only 3-0 team, apologies to Steve Briscoe for becoming the leagues only 0-3 team.  Although I can't tease Steve too much this week, since I was about 1 Doug Jolley completion away from being 0-3 as well.  Lots of parity in the league still as 5 of the 7 matchups this week were decided by 8 points or less.  Believe it or not, I scored the most points this week with a meager 85.60.

On to the recaps:

Cincinnati Hustler (1-2) v. Top Shelf (1-2)

I never thought I had a chance in this one, so I didn't bother watching the Monday Night game.  I was certain Jolley would catch a TD and it would be over.  As a matter of fact the only time I switched to the game was with less than 2 minutes to go in the first half and Jolley caught 3 passes in a row.  Kudos to John for the call to start Reggie Wayne over Driver who was questionable.  24 points later, John was well on his way to victory.  Bret Favre brought me back in it with a late run to try and tie the game, love the prevent defense.  An interception in the end zone hurt, but an unexpected Todd Heap TD and a few Wilkins field goals and I was back on top.  For John, Maddox performed well again, however Jerome Bettis took a TD from Maddox and Zereoue.  Where Wayne excelled, Harrisson faltered, and still no running game for Top Shelf.  My streak of no TDs from my WRs and RBs continues, 1 overall in 3 weeks.  Next week, I face my favorite Tenacious D, although it looks like someone needs a new QB.

Steeles 03 (1-2) v. Wildwood Old School (2-1)

Key injuries to RBs was the story in this one as Portis was limited and Faulk went down.  Lucky for Chris, he has Gordon on his bench ready to step in, although still some drop off from Faulk to Gordon.  For John, I really though he would be able to overtake Chris on MNF, but Sharpe and Portis fell short, mostly due to the injury,  Both QBs performed well and continue to be the strength of their teams.  Bit of a suprise to see John drop San Fran's Defense as they have been really strong so far this season.  

Tenacious D (2-1) v. Super Chargers (2-1)

Not quite the matchup I expected from my #1 and #2 ranked teams, although who expected Culpepper to miss the 2nd half and Bledsoe to follow up his 30+ point weeks with a -3.09.   Damn Miami defense.  Yates attention to the free agent wire has paid off a bit with Bryson at RB and Seattle's Defense.  Both did well this week, but Andre Johnson was the real story with 20.60 points.  Steve King couldn't figure out who Johnson was, much less that he was capable of a 20 point day.  Todd, this week I will be quiet about the Bledsoe - Moulds thing, maybe the'll get back on track against Philly.  Nice to see Tomlinson getting back to form for Tenacious D, although doesn't help much when your WRs put up a combined 2.10 points.  Although, to be fair to Steve, he did have 4 players on bye this week.  Gotta love squeeking out a win with half your team on the bench.  Next week, Steve could struggle with Testeverde at QB, watch for Steve to pick up someone from free agency, Tim Couch anyone?

4th and Inches (1-2) v. The Balance Cheats (1-2)

Andrew's fall from the top seed continued again this week with a poor 56 point effort.  Manning got back on track, but everyone else decided to take the day off.   Not much more to say than that, no one player did anything special worth mentioning.  Shaun Alexander's wife gave birth to a baby girl, so he's got that going for him, which is nice.  You knew he was going to have a bad week when you found out he named her Heaven.  For Ed, congrats on your first victory, that 6 way tie for the 8 spot is getting interesting, huh?  As mentioned last week, a decision to go with Bulger (not that he had a choice) and his big three paid off.  Tampa D and Coles played well, although McCallister failed to show up with only 8 rushing yards.  8?  Did I miss an injury here?  At least he had a better 2nd half, his first half numbers were 5 carries for -9 yards, ouch.  Still like Ed's team here, strong all the way around with good depth.

End Zone Gang (0-3) v. Syracuse Orangemen (3-0)

Best record vs. the worst record, no suprise in the outcome.  In Steve's defense he was here in Cincinnati last weekend, and was obviously distracted by his new granddaughter.  So distracted that he forgot to pick up a WR and was forced to start Thrash who was on a bye.  That could have been the difference maker as he fell less than 5 points short.  Miami's defense played excellent and earned an impressive 17 points.  Other than that, not much else went well, Brady didn't throw much and was sacked 5 times, Dillon got hurt and only earned 26 yards.  For Marty, a big win despite a 6 point effort from his starting QB.  Marty even had 3 TDs sitting on his bench.  If he can continue to win like this and then get Mike Vick back from injury, Marty is soon going to become the team to beat.   Jamal Lewis continued to dominate with a 100+ yard game and another TD.  Nice way to followup a 295 yard day.  I never thought I would find myself checking the free agent wire to see if Pittman was available, but he isn't, he's just sitting around adding more depth to Marty's already deep team.

Chasing the Boilers (1-2) v. Wildcats II (2-1)

Poor Scott, no matter what he does, he can't get any respect from the commissioner for his team.  I've been down on him from the pre-season report and perhaps unjustified with his 2-1 record.  His team looks good on paper, but his production is still lacking.  One week after bashing Eddie George, he went out and put up a 100 yard, 1 td game to show he still has some juice left. Of course, the very same week, his #1 back only rushed for 7 yards and actually lost points because of an apparent halfback pass which was picked off.  Troy Brown continues to be mediocre despite Sean Salsbury's endorsement for a 100+ yard game and 1 to 2 TDs.  Not quite Sean, sorry.  Trent Green is a good QB and deserves better numbers, I just don't see how a team can put up over 40 points in a week and the QB only gets 1 TD.  For Doug, more of the same, Tim Brown - bad.  Priest Holmes - great.  Rich Gannon - not MVP quality like last year.  Bubba Franks - Not the best tight end despite Wesley Walls injury.  Janikowski - in Jail.   Someone else needs to step up if Doug is going to get back in the win column.  Congrats Scott on the win, best of luck making me look bad next week!

Bubb Rubb Allstars (2-1) v. Palmer MVP (2-1)

Can anyone stop Rae Buck and his point machine Palmer MVP?  Another week of good numbers and he even got in a little jab at me with Bettis taking quality carries away from Zereoue.  Not to mention a TD.  Rae got a TD from all his starting RBs and WRs, the exact opposite of me.  Ward is THE most consistant WR in football these days, Peter Warrick appears to have become a decent #3 WR, Ricky Williams has been well worth the #1 pick I questioned early on.  Especially after the performance of the #2 and #3 picks in Faulk and Tomlinson.  I jinxed Crumpler, sorry Rae.  Garcia had an off week and may be suffering from lingering injuries.  For Loren, a good showing that came down to a turnover at the end of the MNF game which could have turned into a much needed Elam field goal.  Brooks was efficient again, but still doesn't put up the 30 passes that are needed to win week in and week out.  All Loren's WRs also reached the endzone and it finally looks like Loren might be able to put up a team this week as 4 of his WRs are on a bye thanks to some wheeling and dealing.  And he didn't even have to give up his waiver position for it.

So, another week gone by, everyone still appears to be in the race, except maybe last years regular season champ Steve.  Big matchup to watch this week is Palmer MVP vs. Wildwood Old School.  Although Rae is without Ricky Williams and Chris is without Faulk.  Lots of byes this week, so expect more free agent action and some possible steals for those willing to sacrifice a waiver position.  Here are this week's Power Rankings:

1) Tenacious D (2-1)
2) Syracuse Orangemen (3-0)  
3) Wildwood Old School (2-1)
4) Palmer MVP (2-1)  
5) Super Chargers (2-1) 
6) Bubb Rubb Allstars (2-1) 
7) Top Shelf (1-2) 
8) Steelers 03 (1-2)
9) The Balance Cheats (1-2) 
10) Wildcats II (2-1) 
11) 4th and Inches (1-2) 
12) Cincinnati Hustler (1-2)
13) Chasin the Boilers (1-2)  
14) End Zone Gang (0-3) 

Until next week,

The Commish

2003.label: Week 4
2003.text:
What fun this weekend was, huh?  Waiver positions were sacrificed, bye weeks killed some top contenders, the commissioner's report put the hex on a couple squads, Loren had his team pillaged, some huge offensive production and some great Monday night comebacks.  And I had the best seat in the house as I got to watch my overstressed brother panic at each occurance.  Those of you who think I am into this league need to spend 6 hours with Loren on Sunday watching NFL Sunday Ticket.  Rae, sorry about the cover jinx last week, I had no idea I was that powerful.  Congrats on destroying Steve Briscoe's record low of 39.51 points.  I realize you had Ricky Williams on a bye, but come on 24.86 points.  You realize there were 13 individual players started this week who would have beat you by themselves.  Peyton Manning would have beat you in the first quarter alone.  More apologies to Todd Yates, Marty Hansen and Steve King.  Its gotta suck to lose when you put up over 100 points, especially when you lose it in the 2nd half of the Monday night game.  Yates almost made it a hattrick on the comebacks thanks to the Packers.  Ahman Green, Favre, Franks and the Packers D all came up huge on MNF.  Go Bears, nice stadium, welcome to the land of great stadiums with awful teams (See Bengals and Reds).  Anyway, on to the recaps.

Bubb Rubb Allstars (2-2) v. Wildcats II (3-1)

If Loren would have been able to pull off a victory this week it would have been a miracle.  He had all his WRs, his top back and his top defense on a bye in week 4.  Some would say thats bad drafting, but thats not my place.  I give Loren credit, he wheeled and dealed and played the waiver wire to the best of his ability and still put an average roster on the field.  Of course, the problem is most of his starters were still average.  Your not going to win many games with Brooks and William Green.  To add to the contreversy this week, Loren learned some lessons about how the waiver system works.  Apparently, you can't make a free agent claim the same day as the player you are dropped played.  Due to this little restriction, Loren lost his top defense, NY Giants to Scott Zide.  In addition, Loren decided his waiver position was worth sacrificing for Brad Johnson, a 3rd QB casualty of Ed's.  This left Loren in a position to lose T.J. Duckett to John Briscoe.  Loren made the call to go with Joe Burns over Duckett the day before Atlanta declared him the starter benching Warrick Dunn.  Wow, tough week and I haven't even gotten to the game yet.  The only bright spot for Loren was Bobby Shaw who has taken the #2 WR spot in Buffalo from Josh Reed.  Shaw is a player Loren will be able to get value out of the rest of the year.  Outside of Shaw, it was all Wildcats.  Scott continued his 3 game win streak with a solid victory behind an improving Jake Plummer.  Torry Holt continued to shine as a top WR, and Scott received an unexpected boost from free agent pick up Anthony Thomas.  Although not a lot of carries, still a 100+ yards and a touchdown.  Although by that point, Scott had already one the matchup.  George was back to normal, but Scott continues to spat in my face at his low Power Ranking.  Looks like we have a candidate for this week's jinx.

Chasin the Boilers (2-2) v. Syracuse Orangemen (3-1)

Another victory for the Commissioner's report.  The only undefeated team was knocked off after some positive recognition in last week's report.  Although he wasn't the top ranking, that distinction went to Tenacious D who was also defeated. :)  This matchup was the closest of the week, lost and then won again in the final moments of the MNF game with a pick on a deflected Kordell Stewart pass with only seconds to go.   Doug had a nice rebound performance from Rich Gannon and Tim Brown which was much appreciated given Priest Holmes' failure to find the endzone for the first time in like 15 weeks.  Slight exaggeration, but not by much.  The only mistake that Marty made this week was taking a chance on Edge playing Sunday night.  He ended up watching from the sidelines which left Marty without a backup RB to play.  Much needed points it turns out.  Other than that, this was played to perfection on a week in which he faced numerous players on byes.  Late free agent signee John Kitna was absolutely huge with 41 points, nice call Marty.  Jamal Lewis continued to shine as either the #1 or #2 back in the league depending on who you ask with another 100+ yards and a touch.  And Tony Gonzalez finally got into the endzone with his 1st TD of the year.  Great matchup and great win for Doug, although Marty won't drop much in the rankings with this one.

End Zone Gang (0-4) v. The Balance Cheats (2-2)

The annual matchup between my father and my father in law turned out to be a sleeper thanks to Marc Bulger.  Ed received great performances from his QB, and both his running backs.  Nice to see Hambrick starting to turn into a consistant back, this makes Ed even more dangerous with an already tough lineup.  Only bad thing that happened was only 1 catch and 4 yards for Derrick Mason, did he get hurt?  Coles slowed down a bit as well, perhaps it was my report last week as well.  For Steve, I've done about everything I can to help him out.  Two weeks in a row at the 14 spot in the Power Rankings wasn't enough to surge him like it did for me.  We'll give it one more shot this week and keep our fingers crossed that Terrell Owens shuts his mouth and starts making plays.  Looks like his erratic play started to show up earlier than expected as his counterparts Moss and Harrison surged while Owens cried on the sidelines.  At least Tai Streets continues to be consistant.  Steve will be in trouble again next week with Dillon most likely out and Betts seeing less and less carries.  Steve will need to find some carries in free agency if he wants to compete.

4th and Inches (2-2) v. Super Chargers (2-2)

In my opinion, Andrew was lucky to escape this week with a win.  Yates almost pulled the comeback on MNF with a 176 yard, 2 TD performance by Ahman Green.  I really thought he had it when they lined up on the 1 yard line after a pass interference call in the end zone.  Instead, Favre decided to throw it to Franks deep in the endzone, and the victory went to Andrew and Peyton Manning.  To be honest, I don't think Andrew is even paying attention to the league which is frustrating.  He started Shaun Alexander who was on a bye, not sure if that was intentional or not.  The real stars however were Manning and the Colts suprising D.  Manning through for an astonishing 6 TD passes and 58 points.  I believe thats a record, but I seem to remember Gannon and Brady putting up 50+ point games last year as well.  For Yates, it was nice to see Bledsoe bounce back.  Almost all his players had decent games, just a little trouble getting touchdowns.  Todd will face Steve and his 0-4 Gang next week while Andrew comes to Cincinnati to face the Hustler.

Wildwood Old School (3-1) v. Palmer MVP (2-2)

Faulk's injury could turn out to be a blessing for Chris as he was finally able to get some production from his RBs.  Gordon had a decent game and Garner found the end zone as well.  Although, the only player Chris needed to start was McNair who beat Rae single handedly.  McNair was a remarkable 15-16 passing with 3 TDs.  Only one incompletion, thats amazing.  To think, McNair was a 7th round pick.  I still absolutely love Chad Johnson, only 3 catches, but 2 TDs.  Its amazing how much trash he talks in the Cincinnati papers, according to him, he is going to be a star.  In the realm of 1800 yards in a season, a feat only accomplished once by Jerry Rice.  I think he needs to average like 140 yards per game the rest of the way to break that mark.  Good Luck, but great pick Chris.  *JINX*  Nothing more to say about Rae, I put the hex on him last week and as a result not one TD for all his starters.  But fear not Rae, Williams is back next week and you get to face the 3-1 Wildcats.  Oops, oh well, good luck anyway.

Steelers 03 (1-3) v. Top Shelf (2-2)

To be honest, I'm a little suprised at John Stafford's 1-3 record.  In his defense this week, Portis was injured and his starting QB was on a bye.  Quincy Carter just doesn't inspire fear into his opponents.  Boldin put up 7 catches and decent yardage again, but no touchdowns.  At least Quincy Morgan finally found the endzone thanks to an early pass from interim QB Couch.  Carolina's D will continue to upset me everytime they allow 3 points and the Steelers D allows 40, BP, huh John Briscoe?  John would have actually been better off benching his RBs as Faulk earned negative points due to limited yardage and a fumble.  For John Briscoe, a nice victory thanks to 3 TDs and 158 yards for Marvin Harrison.  John made a gutsy move that backfired starting Ramsey over Maddox.  I suppose he was trying to show other teams that he has some value, doubt the trade offers are funneling in now.  John's fingers are crossed that a Vick return will give Peerless Price a spurt, does that happen this week or next?  Jolley's TD was one week too late.  By the way, Loren's still pissed and wants Duckett back.  Anyone need Jay Fiedler.

Cincinnati Hustler (2-2) v. Tenacious D (2-2)

I'll be honest, this week everything was clicking.  I went from only 2 TDs all year from my offense, to 9 in one week.  Favre 3 TDs, Moss 3 TDs, Lelie another TD, Taylor and Zereoue - TD.  I was about ready to dump Zereoue after watching Bettis steal his carries last week.  Thanks to Loren for convincing me to start him over Ricky Williams.  It would have worked either way, but I would be without a back next week.  Free agent pick up San Fran turned out to be a bust, no one can stop Minnesota's offense apparently.  Curtis Conway is awful, when is Pennington back again?  For Steve, again, tough loss.  No one expects to lose after putting up 108 points.  Great call on Couch over Testeverde while Culpepper was out.  Tomlinson is officially back, he even threw a TD this week.  Best backfield in the league came to play in week 4.  Although the top seed lost, still a great team and definitely a contender come playoff time.  Sorry about the top ranking, I'll take you off this week.

So that does it for Week 4, lets hope the offense continues to find its groove in week 5.  Here are this week's Power Rankings: 

1) Wildwood Old School (3-1)
2) Syracuse Orangemen (3-1) 
3) Tenacious D (2-2) 
4) The Balance Cheats (2-2)
5) Wildcats II (3-1) 
6) Palmer MVP (2-2) 
7) Super Chargers (2-2)  
8) Top Shelf (2-2) 
9) Cincinnati Hustler (2-2)
10) 4th and Inches (2-2) 
11) Bubb Rubb Allstars (2-2) 
12) Chasin the Boilers (2-2) 
13) Steelers 03 (1-3)  
14) End Zone Gang (0-4)

2003.label: Week 5
2003.text:
Ok, lesson learned... no matter how old your child is, no matter how few hours she sleeps during the night, never turn off MNF before the game is over.  All I can say is I got lucky.  I turned off the TV when it was 28-7 Bucs, Manning had a high completion percentage, but not nearly enough points to overcome my 50 point lead.  The Red Sox won, everybody's happy right?  So, imagine my suprise during the 6:00am feeding when I see a stat showing how no team down by more than 21 points with less than 4 minutes to play has ever come back to win, until now.  Oh crap, if I lost to Andrew who doesn't even play FF anymore (based on his decision to start a player who is OUT for the 2nd straight week), I'm gonna be pissed.  So, like any good parent, I immediately tore the bottle from Katie's mouth, swooped her up so we could check fantasy.  Wheew!!!  We both stopped crying when we realized we snuck by with a 4 point win.  Back to feeding, lesson learned.  

Other than that, not that many suprises this week, 4 of the top 5 teams in the power rankings won, the exception being Ed who came very close to a comeback against Doug, still another respectable showing, especially given his preferred QB, Bulger, was on a bye.  Steve finally won his first game, you can thank me later for placing you at the bottom of the power rankings.  This week, its your turn John Stafford.  Mainly because I play Steve and don't want to give him a win.  A couple of questionable starts at QB this week, one paid off, one was just a bad call.  Brees over Brady, nice job.  Fiedler over B. Johnson, bad call.  Obviously some people pay too much attention to fantasy prediction sites and try to play matchups a little too close.  My opinion, always play your good players, sooner or later they will come around.  See Terrell Owens this week, finally scored a TD.  As far as reading injury reports, one thing you have to keep in mind, the coach is trying to keep the opposing team off guard, so they don't typically say how the player is really feeling until right before the game.  I find that Chris Mortensen's report at the beginning of ESPN Sunday Countdown is pretty reliable, plus sometimes you have to pay for quality data.   Yahoo! is always out of date, I use a seperate site and here are a couple of postings that would have helped this week:

PRICE SAYS HE'LL PLAY - Posted Saturday, October 4, 2003 at 7:05pm EDT.
JAMES GAME-TIME DECISION, DID NOT PRACTICE SATURDAY - They went on to recommend sitting him this week against Tampa's D.

It all depends how into it you are, some are more than others obviously.  Some get calls from players wives with updates apparently.  On to the recaps.

Cincinnati Hustler (3-2) v. 4th and Inches (2-3)

Watch out now, look who has the most potent offense in the league. *knock on wood*  The Cincinnati Hustler have a league high 451 total points.  Favre, Moss and Fred Taylor are all finally clicking after 5 weeks.  Outside of those three, there isn't much else to write about.  Zereoue isn't getting the carries or the goal line opportunities. Lelie is only good for 3 to 4 receptions, you just hope one or two of them is a deep bomb.  Pittsburgh's once dominant defense is as soft as they come these days.  Damn you Carolina D!!!  As for the owner formerly known as Andrew, its all Peyton Manning.  50+ last week, 40+ this week.  Andrew would have had a win this week if he'd have been paying attention and started Conwell over Josh Norman was listed as OUT on the injury report.  Anybody know of GMs who want a team for next season?

Steelers 03 (1-4) v. Tenacious D (3-2)

Maybe if you change your name back to Go Steelers, you'll start winning.  With a name like Steelers 03, you are destined to play as well as the Steelers play which isn't very good either.  How about these names:  Colts 03, Chiefs 03 or Vikings 03 or aim high and go with Dolphins 72.  Or maybe, Fighting Irish 03... no, wait.  :) Had to throw that one in there.  I know.. I know.. (INSERT ILLINOIS JOKE HERE)  Anyway, the only bright spot for John was Clinton Portis who had over 200 yards total offense.  Emmitt Smith has a broken collerbone or something, although you are probably better off without him given his performance so far this season.  Not to mention, Kevin Faulk's injury and solid day by backup Mike Cloud and Antowain Smith.  One thing I will say, I still wouldn't start Quincy Carter over Hasselbeck, it has to be a fluke, right?  For Steve King, another impressive victory behind Tim Couch and Stephen Davis.  As I said in the preseason report, Steve has the best depth at RB in the entire league.  Even during off games for Tomlinson, he has 12 points from Davis and 17 from Moe Williams on his bench.  It also helps to have your #1 WR throw a TD.  If Culpepper is back next week, who will you start Couch or Culpepper?

Wildwood Old School (4-1) v. Top Shelf (2-3)

Congratulations to Chris for surviving the Commish Report Power Rankings Jinx.  Chris remains in the top spot after another solid victory this week.  Chris must have a decent news source as he started all the right players.  McNair over Collins, Porter on the bench with an injury, Onterrio Smith in the lineup and a decent game, although its still tough when you have 3 RBs sharing the load.  Also, nice pickup on the Vikings defense to fill in for Baltimore on their bye week.  Next week, Chris gets his Rams RBs back and McNair facing the Texans.  John Briscoe's great draft strategy showed a few holes this week.  The Steelers continued to fall apart as Maddox was held to negative points.  Still no solid RBs even with the addition of Duckett.  Also, you still wouldn't have won even if you started Price, so don't sweat it too much.  Although, nice to see Price with a good game, Vick should be back soon.  Perhaps you should trade one of your top WRs for an RB?  I'll take Harrison for Taylor?  

End Zone Gang (1-4) v. Super Chargers (2-3)

Again, congrats to Steve for his first win, tough loss again for Yates who continues to put up 80+ point performances yet three straight losses.  I promise Moulds will catch another Bledsoe TD sooner or later.  Most likely, the first week you bench Bledsoe for Jeff Blake.  Note: I don't recommend that.   I'm still mad that you took Ahman Green with the pick ahead of me in the draft.  While I'm happy with Fred Taylor so far, Green has been unstoppable *jinx*.   What happened to Dante Stallworth?  He used to be good for a solid 10 points each week, thats two weeks in a row with only 1 catch.  Steve, great call on starting Brees over Brady, can't say I'd recommend it against anyone other than the Jags D however.  Nice to see an early TD from Owens, although I did notice a couple of drops that could have been TDs.  Its a shame that Streets shuts down as Owens picks up, you hope they could both excel.  Nice to see Shockey with 11 receptions, no other TE is capable of that.

Chasin the Boilers (3-2) v. The Balance Cheats (2-3)

A big win for Doug over the Balance Cheats despite another awful performance from his QB Gannon.  Another one of those decisions, can you really start Harrington over Gannon?  I still think the stars will come out of it sooner or later.  He was the MVP last year after all.  Plus, Priest Holmes went another week without a TD.  Must have been my comments about how far Doug can go behind Gannon and Holmes.  Doug didn't need their help this week, he had 6 catches and a TD from Warrick Dunn, 5 Field Goals from Janikowski, another good performance from Green Bay's Defense who we all laughed at during the draft.  David Boston returned to the lineup and his steroid treatments for 14 catches, 2 TDs and 181 yards.  All that and a humiliating defeat of my beloved Illini.  Its nice to see the equality Illinois shows by letting their women's team play for them on defense.  For Ed, another poor effort from McNabb.  You know, I think the media hypes McNabb up because he is black.  :) He isn't that good of a QB.  Just ask Chris how many times last season he wished he would have started Trent Green over McNabb.   He doesn't stink because of the color of his skin, he stinks becuase of his nasty afro and goatee.  Not to mention his receivers are James Thrash and Todd Pinkston.   Oh well, Bulger is back next week.  Also, kind of scary to see Tampa's defense give up 38 points, at least they still force turnovers and score on defense.  If my calculations are correct, Ed lost the game on the final field goal.  35 points allowed is -1 point, 38 points allowed is -4 right?  Ouch, thats tough, and I thought I was shocked in the morning.  Note: I'm not resigning as commissioner because of my comments, don't even ask.

Bubb Rubb Allstars (2-3) v. Syracuse Orangemen (4-1)

So, after 5 weeks and numerous phone calls with Loren, I finally came to this conclusion.  The Bubb Rubb Allstars aren't that bad.. its their GM that's awful.   Heheheh...  Fiedler over Johnson, come on.  Fiedler shouldn't be a starting QB in the league.  I couldn't believe you took him in the draft over Kelly Holcombe.  Not that that turned out to be a good pick either, but my point is he was bad then, he's bad now.   Plus you've picked up every running back whose ever gained 50 yards in a week, then dropped them the following week before their big 100 yard game.  I'm just kidding, I don't mean to pick on Loren, I just know his thought process for each decision as he likes to call me before each one.  He did make some good calls on Dallas' D, and starting Green over Buckhalter.  Marty won the matchup thanks to McCardell's 3 TDs.  Although it didn't give him credit for his defensive TD on the Mike Doss fumble, not sure how they scored it, I think the points went to Tampa's defense.   Marty's running out of time on his QB situation, Vick still might be a couple weeks away, and Kitna is on a bye next week.  Wonder who he'll pick up on the free agent wire?  Steve Briscoe, can you believe the numbers Pittman is putting up, he was awful when you needed him last year.  Back to back TD weeks from Gonzalez, still not worthy of his early draft position, but who am I to judge, Marty is 4-1 and I am 3-2.  

Wildcats II (4-1) v. Palmer MVP (2-3)

And finally, its official, Scott's team is good.  I fought it all season long and now I will join the Wildcats bandwagon and say that any 4-1 team has to have some talent.  *jinx*  Plummer has turned into a solid option at QB week in and week out.  Anthony Thomas put up his 2nd straight 100+ yard performance.  Eddie George is still rotten.  Then again, maybe its just luck.  3 catches and a TD for Keyshawn.  2 catches and a TD for Troy Brown.  Hmmm... not really the same as Marvin Harrison's 11 catches and multiple TDs.  Another example where having a good news source helps make the calls on who to start.  Travis Henry's 18 points on the bench hurts.  Rae could care less about Fantasy Football right about now.  His Red Sox came back from 0-2 to win the series and now face the Yankees in the ALCS.  GO SOX!!! *knock on wood*  Sorry, really don't want to jinx that one, I HATE the Yankees.  Nice to see Jimmy Smith back in the lineup and that Byron Leftwich seems to like him as the #1 WR, 8 catches for 137 yards.  Ricky Williams was shut down this week, but still managed a TD despite only 39 yards on the ground.  I also heard Pennington started throwing this week and may not be too far off.  Sorry about the comments on Crumpler and Ward, they both have been quiet of late.  

So, going into Week 6, a real clash of the titans at the top of the Power Rankings.  Wildwood Old School will face Tenacious D, and the Wildcats will face the 4-1 Syracuse Orangemen.  By the way, just read that Charles Rogers has a broken clavacle, sorry Andrew.  At least he was on a bye next week.  Odds are Andrew will start him anyway.  

Here are this week's Power Rankings: 

1) Wildwood Old School (4-1)
2) Syracuse Orangemen (4-1) 
3) Tenacious D (3-2) 
4) Wildcats II (4-1)
5) Cincinnati Hustler (3-2)
