2003.label: Week 6
2003.text:
Alright, you waited long enough.  Sorry about the delay, as hard as it may seem, work has been really busy this week.  I was out of town on Monday and Tuesday and my mother is in town this week, plus I'm going through mild depression from the Cubs and Red Sox losses.   With that said, here is another condensed Commissioners report for week 6.

So, last week featured a couple clashes of the titans with last years #1 and #2 coming out on top.  I won a game in which there is no way in hell I deserved to win given the way my team fell apart.  Lucky for me, I was facing Steve :)  John Stafford is still really bad despite the fact that I put him at the bottom of the power rankings, which for the most part has helped teams this year.  Look at me, I won 4 in a row after being last.   Chris continues to spit in the face of the Power Rankings jinx.  Steve King and his wife had another child, which obviously distracted him in his matchup.  Loren finally started the right QB, even though it took about 3 days and 25 instant messaging conversations to convince him to go with Johnson.  Rae Buck got back in the winners circle as T.J. Duckett came short for John Briscoe on Monday Night.  Here are some quick recaps:

Wildcats v. Orangemen

Scott's win over Marty was led by a well deserved 40+ point effort for Trent Green.  Green has the most high powered offense in the league, yet he rarely puts himself in the Peyton Manning, Rich Gannon (last year) category for production.  Torry Holt stole the show on MNF, and they single handedly were able to knock off Marty.  Marty's team has started to sag a bit as he continues to struggle to find a replacement for Mike Vick who may be further off than Marty had planned when he drafted him.  While its worked early on with folks like Brunell and Kitna, Doug Johnson fell on his face.  Next week, Marty will try and send out Vinne Testeverde who had a great week last week off the bye.  Good Luck with that one Marty.

Cheats v. AllStars

Father vs. Son, and the father showed he was wiser.  As I said before, Loren couldn't have asked for a better performance from Johnson, and William Green finally kicked into gear giving Loren his needed 2nd running back.  However, it stops there, depth was the problem this week.  His WRs were quie and his TE was injured leaving the backup with 2 scores.  90 points is good, don't get me wrong, but Ed has great depth at all positions.  Bulger is consistantly good, his backs put up 7-10 points in off weeks, Johnnie Morton had a well deserved boost, Tampa's D put up 22, well worth their early selection.  Next week, Ed might finally get his 3rd WR back, Kevin Curtis.  Who?  Yep, the Rams slot receiver who Ed decided was more valuable three weeks ago than his 3rd QB Brad Johnson.  

Boilers v. Chargers

This matchup was almost as ugly as mine.  Another close shave for Doug who was bad anyway you look at it.  Lucky for him, Yates was worse.  Moulds was out, Bledsoe has collapsed, and Philly's D is nowhere near the defense it was last year. At least Ahman Green is one of the best backs in the league, actually the best so far if you ask me.  For Doug, a 4-2 record has to make him happy as he literally is chasin his boilers and their 5-1 record.  Gannon's team is awful and may be worth looking for a new #2, but at least he was able to muster decent numbers.  Priest Holmes found the endzone after a couple weeks off and Bubba Franks is doing exactly what Doug expected... catching 1 yard TDs.  Better than Todd Heap who hasn't done anything with Kyle Boller.  Or Shockey for that matter.   

Palmer v. Top Shelf

Where did Tommy Maddox and the Steelers go?   At least you still have Harrison and Driver.  Peerless Price unfortunately performs better on the bench, and kudos on another 25 point effort for your defense.  I have yet to break the 10 point barrier with mine.  For Rae, I really feel for you, Grady Little is a bad manager.  I guess in a way you should feel proud for what the Red Sox accomplished depsite his managerial decisions.  On the fantasy field, a good win with balance from all your starters.  Garcia struggled, but 6, 7, 8, 9 points from your WRs and RBs will get you a win in this league.   I'm mad about the Dominick Davis thing, now I'm stuck on a week with both my RBs on byes and Stacey Mack left with the #2 job.  I picked him up at one point, but didn't have the free roster spots to keep him.  My loss, good pickup for a Bettis replacement.  

Old School v. Tenacious

At least you had a baby this week...  although knowing Steve's commitment the reward level between a win and a child is closer than it should be.  Don't get me wrong, I know the feeling, I had my eye on the Giants-Cowboys MNF game while holding Gretchen's leg during pushing.   Its sick, but it helps to admit we all have a problem.  Don't laugh, we know who you are...  Loren, Chris, John Briscoe, your with us.    54 combined points for the defenses in this matchup.  Wow!  31 for the Rams, never saw that coming.  Good news for Steve is that he gets Culpepper back this week.  Couch's has done well, but not well enough.   Chris just keeps riding McNair, all the way into first place.  Hey Marty, I finally know how you felt last year.  Frustrated about how GMs just hog good players on their bench without any intention of ever starting them.  Then, even when you attempt to trade, the door is shut immediately.  We shortened the benches this year to avoid this reoccurance, but Steve apparently didn't get the memo.  QUIT HOGGING ALL THE RBS, I'm desperate for one this week.  I can't believe I'm actually going to start Stacey Mack and Adrian Peterson!!!  Then again, in Steve's defense, maybe he will find a way to start Duce Staley, Moe Williams, Mike Cloud, Deshawn Foster, Stephen Davis and Ladanian Tomlinson.   JERK!!!!


Steelers v. 4th and Inches

Ok...  I talked to Andrew this weekend and he does read my reports and he is paying some attention.  He did win after all.  Although, I know its not my place to say it, but its too funny to avoid it.  With Peyton on a bye this week, he picked up Doug Johnson.  Thats all I'll say for now, drink up buddy.   John Stafford, maybe Bulger will get hurt and Warner will be the comeback player of the year.  And maybe Charlie Batch will replace Maddox and the Steelers will turn it around?  I talk a lot about how disappointed I am in myself for taking the Steelers D over Carolina, but at least I feel good about taking Favre over Hasselbeck.  Thanks for that!

Hustler v. the Gang

Thanks Jeff Wilkins for the field goal with 3:50 to play.  Martz could have given up with a lead like that, but he knew I needed the points.  Of course, I'll be honest I was in a hotel in Portland and I fell asleep when it was 17-0.  So I didn't have a clue about it until the next morning.  Maybe thats why I won, after all it was 4-0 when I started watching the Sox last night.  The only reason I won this game was Bret Favre.  He continues to put up big numbers week in and week out.  Moss was on a bye so I was left with my below par WR core of Lelie, Conway and Ferguson.  Taylor wasn't great, Zereoue has all but become the #2.  Talk about no depth, again lucky to be 4-2.  Steve is desperate to dump Owens, Brady is just plain bad this year, Betts and Barlow aren't exactly a tough RB core with Dillon hurt.  Miami's D is about the only thing Steve has clicking right now.  

So with all that said, matchup of the week is Wildcats and the 5-1 record vs the Balance Cheats who are only 3-3 but again a much better team on paper.  Here are this week's Power Rankings: 

1) Wildwood Old School (5-1) 
2) Wildcats II (5-1) 
3) Syracuse Orangemen (4-2) 
4) Cincinnati Hustler (4-2) 
5) Tenacious D (3-3) 
6) The Balance Cheats (3-3) 
7) Chasin the Boilers (4-2) 
8) Palmer MVP (3-3) 
9) 4th and Inches (3-3)
10) Top Shelf (2-4) 
11) Bubb Rubb Allstars (2-4) 
12) Super Chargers (2-4) 
13) Steelers 03 (1-5)
14) End Zone Gang (1-5)

Until next time... here's to football.  Boycott the World Series.

The Commish

2003.label: Week 7
2003.text:
I remember talking to Loren about 5 weeks ago in which he was afraid I wouldn't put out the weekly MFFL report if my team continued to play as bad as it did the first two weeks.  I was 0-2 and not showing any signs of life.  Loren was 2-0 and suprising all of us.  Of course, then Bret Farve and Randy Moss decided to start playing.  Byron Leftwich took the helm in Jacksonville and Fred Taylor started to see the end zone again.  Loren's WRs shut down and Tiki Barber remembered that he can't hold on to a football.  The rest is history, a 5 game winning streak for me, a 5 game losing streak for Loren.  The moral of the story is that fantasy football is all about streaks.  I heard Fox advertising the NFL pro bowl ballot this week and one of the commentators mentioned that someone is going to get votes who won't even be playing come January.  See Anquan Boldin, Moe Williams, Rich Gannon or maybe Donovan McNabb.   :)

This week we saw some balance restored to the league.  A 4 way tie for first place, and a lot of 4-3, 3-4 teams.  Then there is John Stafford, who appears to have a good team on paper.  But without a QB who puts up 30+, a 6 game losing streak.  Where's Kurt Warner when you need him?  Steve picked up his 2nd win of the year thanks in part to a resurgence in Terrell Owens.  I know for a fact that 4-5 GMs tried to take him off Steve's hands, but then again we are dealing with Steve the GM.  He wouldn't trade Ladell Betts for his own granddaughter.  Fear not GMs, Owens will have another 2 catch game and Brady will put up negative points and Steve will be right back at it.  

Then there is Andrew Briscoe.  In addition to my own frustration, I've heard complaints from several other GMs.  Its just not fair to people who pay for extra news services, read columns every day, continually monitor free agent wires, draft each round as if it was life and death, and carefully plan matchups week in and week out.  They end up 2-5 while Andrew sports a 4-3 record, wins games starting only 60% of his team, drafts three rounds and sets it to autodraft so he can recover from his hangover.  He actually managed to beat the #1 team in the league this week, starting Manning, Booker, and Candidate.  All of which were out.  Bunch of crap if you ask me, family or not, anyone know someone who wants a team in the MFFL?  Send names to mdmuchnick@yahoo.com.

Speaking of my family, not a bad week.  Ed won, I won, Steve won, John B. won, Andrew won and Loren....  lost...  again.   Come on Loren, you're killing us.  If you keep this up I may just contract the league back to 12.  heheheh, to be fair, his luck is awful.  I think Shawn King came in to wrap up this week, with Loren down by 1 1/2 points.  Ouch.  Anyway, here are some recaps.

Top Shelf v. Tenacious D

I enjoyed this victory as much as John did.  Steve deserves to lose after holding onto 7 quality backs.  Nice to see both Foster and Davis shut out by Tennessee.  Not many more weeks for Williams before Bennett comes back.  Sooner or later, Steve's gonna be calling us saying, Please trade me Amos Zereoue.  Well maybe thats a stretch.  Good news for Steve is Culpepper looked good again, putting up 31 points.  Tomlinson is back in shape as the leagues #1 RB with a 200 yard game.   Outside of that its all falling apart.  Denver is lost without Plummer affecting Rod Smith, Galloway is no longer the #1 target for Carter as Glenn appears to be taking all the catches, and Javon Walker and Robert Ferguson just aren't good #3 options.  For John, it took a strong effort by KC's D on MNF to pull out the win.  A bold move given how well New England's D has performed for him.  A couple of big games from unlikely candidates in Hearst and Steve Smith, now if only his stars could start performing.  

Bubb Rubb v. Super Chargers

So the only thing I could say to Loren is that his team lacks a superstar.  7-8 decent players just doesn't win games apparently.  Johnson had decent numbers, but only 1 TD.  Toomer and Jackson have become quiet recently.  Barber and Green are inconsistant and on teams that don't score much.   The McMichael trade appears to have paid early dividends however and maybe those extra 5 points will be the difference maker.  Yates picked up a much needed win with decent performances by Ahman Green, the league's #1 RB, and Bledsoe.  A late scratch for Moulds made this closer than it needed to be with Santana Moss on the bench emerging as the only receiver in New York.  Stallworth finally got back into the endzone, however the problem is it was his only catch of the game.  Overall a big win, but things aren't looking up for Todd as Bledsoe's numbers still aren't on par with last year.  

Wildcats v. Balance Cheats

Travis Henry and Torry Holt are both great players.  Trent Green is a tough one as he is capable of 40 points one week and 12 the next.  I talked to Scott himself this weekend and even he is suprised at his teams success.  On paper, they aren't great but they find a way to win games.  Of course, he faced the league's #1 underachiever this week, and finally ran out of luck.  Bulger has Ed climbing the standings and all this with 3 TDs on the bench for two weeks in a row.  Last week it was Derrick Mason, this week it was Terry Glenn.  Watch out next week, because its Coles turn.  

Orangemen v. Palmer MVP

I don't know how he does it, but Marty continues to laugh at my analysis that you need a 30 point QB to win in the MFFL.  Marty won again and sports a 5-2 record despite using old, low quality QBs.  He has managed to win with Brunell, Kitna and Testaverde.  The Jags, Bengals and Jets can't even win with those guys.  I'll be honest, I don't think Vick is going to come back and put up 40 points a game, but who cares, right Marty?  Keenen McCardell is playing better than he is, Bruce is putting up big yardage, Jamal Lewis is a top 5 back with 6 straight 100 yard games, Pittman continues to catch 5+ balls a game, and Edge is still riding the bench with injuries.  1st place tie in the standings and the first team to break the 600 point barrier.  Not bad.  Rae looks to be on a bit of an upswing as well despite the loss.  Garcia and Owens are playing better, Pennington comes back this week, Warrick is a legit receiver, and Dominick Davis fills the #2 back role he has been desperately missing.  Add to that Ward and Jimmy Smith coming off byes and you have a team that I don't want to play next week.

Wildwood Old School v. 4th and Inches

Sorry Chris, nothing more that I can say.  Baltimore D looked flat, Gordon got hurt, the Raiders offense is bad, McNair had a tough time with Carolina D despite the score and Andrew got lucky.

Steelers v. End Zone Gang

Brady had a good game, Owens had a good game, Streets and Dillon scored despite poor performances, and Shockey had a TD.
All good things, now on to the bad things for the coming weeks.  Owens is streaky, could be good, could be bad.  Thrash is a bad receiver on a bad offense.  Betts is out for a few weeks.  Dillon still doesn't look 100%.  And finally, you played John Stafford.  If Brady can keep it up, Steve is going to win, if not, hello cellar.  John, I know how hard it is to do, and I know as soon as you make the call Hasselbeck will put up 40, but maybe it's time to give Quincy Carter a shot.  I can't believe I just said that.   In addition, drop Robert Ferguson, he stinks, I rode him 3 weeks and got nothing.  Keep riding Plaxico, he'll come back strong off the bye week.  Portis is a horse, Kevin Faulk isn't.  Neither is Marcell Shipp, try and find some free agent steals.  Perhaps a trade with Steve King.  Good call on Dallas D, but still can't believe you dropped Carolina.  Was that a gift for me or do you know something I don't?  Good Luck.


Hustler v. Boilers

I thought you had me this week Doug.  Down 60 points but with Gannon, Holmes, Janikowski and Tim Brown on MNF, I expected to lose.  I thought it would be a shoot-out and Tim Brown would catch the winning TD to make me eat my words all season long.  But then I remembered Gannon is old, so is Tim Brown, and the Raiders stink.  Nice to see Boston back to form with 2 catches for 10 yards.  Looks like its time to hit the free agent wire for a new QB and Harrington isn't it with Rogers out.  For the Hustler, more big games from Favre, Moss, Heap, and Wilkins.  Bad call on the Jets D, and when will I learn that Conway and Lelie won't do well until there #1 QBs are back.  Took a gamble with Peterson and Henderson at starting RB, but it paid off enough.  I had a feeling about Henderson, even though Stacey Mack did pick up two TDs as a goal line back.  Some people are made to be specialty players.  It felt good to steal 2 TDs from Rae who has been stealing Zereoue TDs all season long with Bettis.  

Stay tuned for next week, I'll post the top 5 smartest comments I've made and the top 5 dumbest.  Sneak peek, "Scott Zides best draft picks were Atlanta's D and J.J. Stokes"...  heheheh.  Also, watch out for the revenge matchup of the week as I face Loren.  Although I got my defense and my RBs are back from the bye week.  Bad news is Bettis will start over Zereoue and Favre is out on a bye and has a broken thumb, how do you throw with a broken thumb?  Amazing.  The other big matchup is the Orangemen vs. The Balance Cheats.

Here are this week's Power Rankings:  

1) Wildwood Old School (5-2) 
2) Syracuse Orangemen (5-2) 
3) Cincinnati Hustler (5-2) 
4) Wildcats II (5-2) 
5) The Balance Cheats (4-3)
6) Tenacious D (3-4) 
7) Chasin the Boilers (4-3) 
8) 4th and Inches (4-3)
9) Top Shelf (3-4)
10) Palmer MVP (3-4) 
11) Super Chargers (3-4)
12) Bubb Rubb Allstars (2-5) 
13) End Zone Gang (2-5)
14) Steelers 03 (1-6)

Until next time...  Keep boycotting the World Series.

The Commish

2003.label: Week 8
2003.text:
All in all a good week for the Cincinnati Hustler.  I was able to win despite starting Byron Leftwich.  The Yankees lost the World Series.  The Rams continue to play well despite Mike Martz.  Grady Little was fired from the Red Sox.  Katie's sleep habits are improving and she's actually starting to smile.  Andrew almost fielded an entire roster for the week.  And the Bengals are actually out of last place.  How does it make you feel John S. that the Bengals are better than the Steelers?  Heeheheh.  

Then the bad news.  Loren was put on suicide watch after losing his 6th straight game.  Doug Evernham finally realized I was right that Gannon is too old (see below) and decided to quit after week 7.  I still start each week with 1 QB, 1 WR, and 1 RB.  How I'm winning still is a mystery to me.  The Boilermakers were stomped in Ann Arbor.  Illinois is officially in last place in the Big Ten behind Indiana and Northwestern.  And I am officially out of the Bachelor pool after Merideth was sent home by Bachelor Bob.   Whoa, wrong column...  Ignore that last one, I meant Al Macinnis is out with a detachd retina.  Yeah, thats what I said.  

Alright, lets get this apathy thing out on the table.  Nothing pisses me off more than people not caring about Fantasy Football.  What else do you really have to do thats more important?  I have a 6 week old daughter, but she knows where she ranks on the priority list.  To hear that Doug was over at the Briscoe's on Sunday watching football and he "forgot" to field a team for the week is absurd.  Steve, John, next time this happens, lock the doors.  You can start it over Thanksgiving when Andrew tries to open the garage door.  Change the code on him, make him field a full team before letting him in the door.  I would rather have 100 Loren's calling me after ever Tiki Barber fumble than one GM who checks the site once a week on Tuesday mornings to see if he won.   Alright, I feel better.

So, this week I'm not going to go through each matchup seperately, just some random thoughts from the past week.  To start, again good win John Stafford.  Congrats on getting over your losing streak and here's to better luck in the second half.  Seriously, Doug aside, it was a good win... 58 points would beat a lot of teams in this league.  To be honest, I actually made a waiver claim for Maddox as well, guess I got lucky there.  Tough to be Clinton Portis right now, without a QB defenses simply key on him leaving you with no real offensive weapons.  What were you thinking dropping Gary Anderson, he was your leading scorer last week.  Hehehehe.  I've said enough about you Doug, I hope Holmes breaks his hip this week.  Another win for Marty in last week's big matchup.  Add another mediocre QB to the list that Marty has won with, David Carr.  Don't know how you do it, but whatever it is keep it up.  Ed continues to underachieve with another game he should have won.  Bulger consistant as ever, but back to back 3 TD performances left the well pretty dry for his receivers.  Coles lack of production for the past 6 weeks or so further emphasizes my feeling that you need to draft players on good teams.  Guys like Coles and Fred Taylor can only do so much on bad teams, while someone like Pittman can do well on a good team when he stinks.  Go figure.

Scott took the lead in total points last week with a solid 100+ point performance.  Torry Holt I can understand, he's a stud this year.  But, Ike Hilliard and Eddie George with huge games.  Sometimes, you just have to admit you got lucky.  Finally, the one week it looks like Scott would be depleted with George, Green, and Henry on bye weeks.  Instead, Chris decides to bail him out and give him Garner, Robinson and Collins for a slew of overachievers in Kitna, George, and Troy Brown.  Not following this one Chris?  Another observation, never name your team after an NFL franchise.  All it does is make you play like them.  If you do make sure its a good team.  See Steelers 03, Super Chargers, last years Bengals 11-5.  For those of you who don't know, you can change your name midway through by clicking on the "Edit team info" button at the very top of the page under your welcome.  

Steve and Rae Buck came down to the wire on MNF last week in a matchup of the top backs.  Ricky Williams vs. Ladanian Tomlinson with Rae up a touchdown.  Who'd have thought Brian Griese would convert Miami to a passing team.  Advantage Steve King.  Rae, I knew picking Ricky over Ladanian would hurt you at some point, sure enough week 8.  Stephen Davis was back on track this week and Domanick Davis continues to be a huge pickup for Rae in Houston.  With Pennington back in the lineup, Ward and Smith still putting up good numbers, and two good backs, Rae is ready for a surge.  Don't think I didn't notice you starting Crumpler on a bye either buddy!  John Briscoe was beaten by his apathetic little brother Andrew.  The loss sent Top Shelf's management into a tailspin making cuts and trading away big players Driver and Curtis Martin.  John, its your own fault, you started Jake Delhomme after all.  Moe Williams joins John's backfield and should help as long as Bennett doesn't steal the starting job.  John's gonna go out on a limb and start Quincy Carter it appears, good luck with that.  I miss Peyton Manning, had him last year through his ups and downs, this years its all ups.

In the Wildwood - End Zone Gang matchup, only two stars came to play, McNair and Chad Johnson.  Neither team had any rushing game.  Steve was saddled after Dillon's "car accident".  Bet that Favre trade looks pretty good right about now, huh Steve.  Got to give it to Steve, three whiners doesn't help any team.  Just remember it was your own son who stole Marvin Harrison from you, pay him back at Christmas by giving your son-in-law all his presents.  I gave you a granddaugter, he gave you an ulcer from Terrell Owens.  And finally, poor Loren and his bad luck.  Hilliard takes all the TDs from Toomer, Buckhalter steals them from Westbrook in the one week he needs himand Green is in the slammer.  The good news is even Randy Moss has dabbled in the dubage and look at him.  Aaron Brooks is starting to play well.  Chambers and McMichael have been rejuvenated by Griese, Barber scored and still puts up good yardage.  But then again, you did play me, Moss and my dominant secret weapon Arlen Harris.  The streak is alive. 

So, that leaves us at the halfway point of the season.  The top 4 teams are starting to seperate from the pack a bit.  St. Louis' overall record is far above Evansville's and Indy's (Loren being the exception).  I thought after listening to me ramble week in and week out, it would nice to see if I actually said anything of value.  With that, here are the top 5 smartest and top 5 dumbest things I've said this season.

Top 5 Smartest:

1) [Doug's] selections like Tim Brown and Tyrone Wheatley.  Brown struggled to do well last year as the #2 receiver in Oakland and this year has moved down the depth chart behind Jerry Porter.  Wheatley may not even be the 4th best back in Oakland behind Garner, Crockett and possibly Justin Fargas.
2) Rae's best pickup may have been Hines Ward in the 3rd round.
3) If you find yourself lacking in QB towards week 8 or 9, Ed's your guy with McNabb, Brad Johnson and Marc Bulger.  It remains to be seen if he can afford to hold three QBs and whether Warner will falter like everyone expects.
4) His top three picks of Ahman Green, Moulds and Bledsoe are strong although they do rely on the success of the Bills offense.  Without Price, Moulds may get too much attention limiting his numbers.
5) Middle of the road QBs like Collins and McNair were available in the later rounds and both can put up the numbers Chris will need to get over the top each week.  I really like Koren Robinson and Chad Johnson,although I think it drops off from there with Derrius Thompson and Todd Pinkston.

2003.text:
Well, it had to come to an end sometime.  It was a good run while it lasted but after 6 straight weeks... Loren won.  How bad do you feel this week John Stafford.  You're still the Bengals of our league, and that makes Loren the Arizona Cardinals.   Oh yeah, my streak is over too, 6 wins in a row, but I met a better team and lossed.  Congrats to Scott, the premier team in the MFFL at a little over halfway.  Yes, I realize Chris is tied for first with a 7-2 record, but come on 716 total points ranks you 10th in the league in total offense.  At some point, you half to say your lucky to keep winning when you score 69 points.  Yes, you beat me head to head, again against my season low 61 points.  Somehow you have the best defense in the league except we don't play defense.  And I stand corrected on that trade, you really proved me wrong.  Troy Brown, -5 yards rushing (he is a reciever right?), Kitna, 58.9 QB rating, and George who did the best for you last week was on a bye.  Bitter you ask, yes, I am.  Kerry Collins lit me up for 35, Charlie Garner, 10 points, and Koren Robinson is still the underachiever he was last week.  

So, before I open the door too much for criticism from Chris, I'll move on to the rest of the league.  Scott Zide had another big game from Hilliard, Holt and Thomas.  Torry Holt continues to be the best receiver in the league surpassing Moss and Harrison in overall production.  With George and Brown gone, he really doesn't have anymore holes to point out.  Like 95% of fantasy leagues out there, Scott was the GM who tried to ride the Mili train after a 2 TD game last week, general rule tight ends never put up back to back big games.  Obvious exceptions being Gonzales and Shockey.  For me, my receivers just plain stink, not to mention that I am desperate for a #2 back at this point.  In a way, I'm just as lucky to be 6-3 right now.  

John Stafford actually had a decent week this week putting up 75+ which would have defeated over half the league.  Of course, Loren finally got real production from his WRs and his new TE continues to give him a bonus 5-10 points.  All his trades are finally starting to pay off.  I hope this streak continues for a bit, it won't be any fun without you in the playoffs trying to start Mike Vick in his first week back from injury.   Doug Evernham, you might as well call it a season right now.  Your starting line-up last week was Harrington, Tim Brown, David Boston, David Terrell, Warrick Dunn and Tyrone Wheatley.   Ouch, at least they were all playing on Sunday.  One positive thing about Chris other than his record.  With McNair, Chad Johnson, Tai Streets, Faulk, and Michael Bennett, he looks to have a solid lineup for the 2nd half.  Add a little luck and he could win out.  *JINX*  One thing I've learned, the more nice things I say, the worse the team does.  

John Briscoe learned another lesson from his father this week, it pays to pick a quality QB in the early rounds in this league.  Not that I'm on the Brady bandwagon just yet, but when your shuffling between Maddox, Carter, and Ramsey all season long you're gonna lose some games.  See my team, my receivers are awful minus Moss but Favre continues to win games for me.  The way Bennett looked this week, I'd be worried about Moe Williams and that trade.   Steve continues to be plagued by his pampered players.  Dillon is more trouble than he's worth and conitnues to eat a roster spot.  Owens gets TDs still, but 2 catches and 17 yards.  Guess it wasn't the QB huh Terrell?  Nice win Steve, slow and steady pulling his way out of the cellar for a playoff push.

Tenacious D continues to improve behind his dominant backfield.  3rd overall in total offense and some bad luck still scares me for the playoffs.  While not #1 in the Power Rankings, he still is one of the teams to beat in my book.   Driver didn't pay off this week, but you'll be happy with that deal in the long run.   For Andrew, the Manning Express took a week off with only 21 points.  Nice to see Booker, Mike Cloud and Conwell still in the lineup...  punk!   Big win for Yates this week, all it took was a Jeff Blake.  Really, Jeff Blake?  That and Santana Moss emerging as the only receiver in New York.  THROW IT TO CONWAY!!!  Oh wait, I dropped him, nevermind.  Marty you should have seen it coming, you aren't capable of winning with a real QB.  If thats what you want to call Aaron Brooks.  Perhaps starting QB would be a better tag.  Especially going against a guy like Blake.  Next week when we face off with Brooks on a bye, I've got the guy for you.   You ready for this...   RICK MIRER!  Trust me.  

Finally nice to see Rae Buck with a big win.  His draft lack of strategy is finally paying off.  Pennington is back in the lineup and getting big points.  Jimmy Smith is the #1 guy in Jacksonville, and Dominick Davis is getting all his endzone carries stolen by Stacey Mack.  Solid receiving core and a top QB make Rae as dangerous as ever.  For Ed, as Bulger goes, so do the Balance Cheats.  An off day led to a tough loss.  Nice to see Laverneous Coles get in the end zone again finally,  That and the guy you've been waiting on all season, Kevin Curits finally had some catches.

During this annual note, I usually offer my congratulations to the winner of the league, while I drown my sorrows in the misery of year after year missing out on winning an MFFL championship. Fun fact, Scott has lost in the championship round 4 times (2002, 2003, 2004, 2023) which seems like a lot, but then again, he is a 4-time champion as well (2007, 2012, 2018, 2021).   That’s 8 out of the 21 years (38%), he’s made the finals.    With that history lesson, let me formally congratulate ME on winning the 2023 MFFL Cup. Dak in Round 7, Tua and Goff in Round 10, Purdy and Mostert in round 12, Cleveland D in round 14, Laporta in round 15 and free agent signings of Puka Nacua, Kyren Willaims and Brandon Aubrey.

This victory marks Loren's third MFFL Championship, adding to his previous wins in 2006 and 2014. He now joins the exclusive 3-timers club with Andrew B, Steve King and Scott Zide who has the record 4 championships.   
The playoffs were nothing short of thrilling. In the quarterfinals, The Skeeters showcased their prowess by eliminating Sunday’s Best with an impressive 174.80 points. Meanwhile, Supersonic Turtles upset Big Booty Jeudy taking them all the way to the 3rd place game. The semifinals saw DolFan Madness outlasting Supersonic Turtles (160.04 to 114.76), and Give Em’ The Beans! overpowering The Skeeters (149.48 to 121.84).  In the battle for third place, The Skeeters narrowly defeated Supersonic Turtles (124.76 to 122.88) and getting into the money. 
During the regular season, DolFan Madness finished the season with an 11-3 record and 1,710.14 PF, earning the Best Record Award. . Give Em’ The Beans! Wasn’t far behind with a 10-4 record and a league best 1,943.02 points, 100 more than the next best team, Supersonic Turtles.  The Skeeters secured the third spot with a 9-5 record and 1,726.54 PF.  As always, I like to let everyone know about my hard luck, finishing with 1774 points (4th highest), yet finishing with a 4-10 record.  That’s more points than DolFan Madness and his league best 11-3 record.   Granted King Will, our rookie manager, did have more points scored on him with 1861, but he also had a 2nd worst in points scored.    Welcome to the League Rookie!   Kudos for his consolation bracket playoff push putting him in 7th place for the final standings.
Looking back at our Keeper selections this year, I know Loren struggled with leaving Justin Jefferson unprotected to secure more value with his Gibbs keeper, but it paid off in the end as he was forced to take Ja’Marr Chase with his 1st pick who will end up with the Triple Crown this year leading in Reception, Yards and TDs.   Breece’s Pieces choice of Nakua with a 15th pick paid off well after several early injuries. Kyren Williams was a stud for Sunday’s Best, Achane was good for DolFan Madness.   However the best decisions had to be from Big Booty Jeudy with Burrow and Barkley.    I though the Burrow decision with an early pick was a bad play, but he proved me wrong with an incredible season, not to mention 2000 yards from Barkley.   
Looking back at the draft, we can continue to throw out the preseason draft grades with both Jack and I receiving A and A+ results but finishing the league in the bottom 2 spots.   Biggest bust had to be McCaffrey with a 1st round keeper killing Tenacious D’s season.     Olave and Pacheco ended up as pretty bad late round 1 picks.      Steals of the draft for me were Brian Thomas Jr. in the 6th for OJ, The Skeeters with Mike Evans as a keeper, always reliable no matter his age.   Jordan Addison in the 8th for King Will, Jameson Williams in the 9th for The Skeeters, McConkey also in the 9th to Andrew B.    Brock Bowers went in the 9th to Tenacious D.  Fun fact, he was taken in the 1st round in my other league and we all laughed at the new manager, but she ended up finishing in 2nd place, losing by a couple points due to the terrible Terry McLaurin final game.   Chuba Hubbard in the 10th to John B, Mooney in the 12th to OJ, Jeudy to me in the 12th but of course I dropped him before he exploded.    Sorry if I missed any other huge steals.   
Hear are the final payouts, they will be sent out as soon as I get all the final payments.
1st Place: Loren Muchnick (Give Em’ The Beans!) - $250
2nd Place: Jeff Ready (DolFan Madness) - $75
3rd Place: Scott Zide (The Skeeters) - $25
Best Regular Season Record: Jeff Ready (DolFan Madness) - $150
Regular Season Most Points – Loren Muchnick (Give Em’ The Beans!) - $100

I said I would do a draft pick selection based on the previous year’s standings but completely forgot this year.   Happy to do it next year but of course I finished in 2nd last so don’t want to enforce it to my benefit.   So, let me know if you want to do this next year. 2025.label: Final Payout Email
2025.text:
Another season is officially in the books, marking our 24th year as the MFFL. As always, it’s time to look back on the highs, the lows, the bad beats, the questionable lineup decisions, and the annual reminder that Yahoo! draft grades remain a complete work of fiction.
Let’s start where we should.
Congratulations to your 2025 MFFL Champion:
You’re My Boy Blue! (Marc Muchnick)
Yes, I’m fully aware how that reads coming from the commissioner, but the standings don’t lie. You’re My Boy Blue! defeated DolFan Madness (Jeff Ready) in the championship game 143.90 to 123.28, completing a strong playoff run and capturing my third MFFL Championship (2003, 2023, 2025). That puts Blue firmly back into the multi-title club and caps off a season where consistency finally translated into playoff success.
Credit to DolFan Madness, who once again proved to be one of the league’s best and most reliable teams, dropping the highest playoff score of the season in the semifinals before running into a deeper roster in the finals. He also led the regular season in total points and finished 10-4.   Finding Nico rounded out the podium with a 3rd place finish, one of the biggest outperformances of the year relative to draft-day expectations.
Playoff Recap
The playoff bracket delivered as usual:
King Will and Finding Nico both came out strong and made quick work in the quarterfinals
DolFan Madness exploded in the semifinals with a 194.20 point performance
You’re My Boy Blue! handled business in both rounds, including a huge upset in the finals.   
Let’s be honest, Jeff had the best team, but his usually reliable starters collapsed when he needed them most.   Waddle got injured, Cook was average and JSN failed to score a TD ending with only 16.2 pts.     Bijan Robinson came through for me clinching the victory on MNF with his 93 yard TD before half.  
Regular Season Awards and Standings
The regular season standings were tight at the top with three teams finishing 10-4, seeded by record first and total points as the tiebreaker.
Best Regular Season Record: DolFan Madness (10-4)
Most Regular Season Points: DolFan Madness (1928.64)
You’re My Boy Blue! finished at 10-4 with 1795.14 points, while our youngest GM, King Will, also posted a 10-4 record but landed just behind on total points.  Tenacious D had the toughest result scoring the 2nd most regular season points but only an 8-6 record due to a league high points against.   He was led by CMC but let down by injured stars like Lamar Jackson and Mike Evans.  Loren Muchnick went from first to last place.   John Briscoe scored a season low in total points (1488.44, 440 less than Jeff Ready).
Draft Day Projections vs Reality
Yahoo projected TheDudeAbides and Tenacious D as league favorites, while You’re My Boy Blue! was slotted 4th and Finding Nico all the way down at 9th. As usual, reality ignored those projections entirely.
Finding Nico deserves special recognition for turning a projected bottom-tier finish into a podium result. On the other end of the spectrum, several highly projected teams never recovered from early injuries or overconfident draft decisions.
Keepers and Roster Construction
Keepers once again shaped the league:
Bijan Robinson anchored my championship roster providing consistency week in and week out.  
Josh Allen and Derrick Henry delivered elite value for Supersonic Turtles
Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Trey McBride formed a positional advantage core for DolFan Madness
Draft Steals, Busts, and Regrets
Steals of the draft:
Drake Maye (Round 11) and George Pickens (Round 5) for You’re My Boy Blue!
Bo Nix (6th Round) for TheDudeAbides
James Cook  (Round 3) delivering elite value for DolFan Madness
Jaylen Warren (Round 7) for Tenacious D
Jakobi Meyers (Round 7) and Javonte Williams (Round 9) for Sunday’s Best
Tyler Warren (9th Round) for The Skeeters
Caleb Williams (10th Round) and Brandon Aubrey (9th Round and actually paid off) for Finding Nico
Busts and disappointments:
Had to be Justin Jefferson, 1st round talent with only 900 yards and 2 TDs, Malik Nabers injury, 2nd round pick for Sunday’s Best. 
Lamar Jackson (2nd round reach) followed up by Marvin Harrison Jr in the 3rd round.
All-Time MFFL Championships (Updated)
With the 2025 season complete, here is the updated all-time championship tally:
Scott Zide – 2007, 2012, 2018, 2021 (4)
Steve King – 2004, 2005, 2008 (3)
Andrew Briscoe – 2011, 2013, 2019 (3)
Loren Muchnick – 2006, 2014, 2024 (3)
Marc Muchnick – 2003, 2023, 2025 (3)
Chris Baumgartner – 2002, 2010 (2)
John Briscoe – 2016, 2022 (2)
Ryan Muchnick – 2022 (1)
Jeff Ready – 2015 (1)
Steve Briscoe – 2009 (1)
Steve Smith – 2017 (1)
Josh Smith – 2020 (1)
All Others (Jack, Greg S., Andrew K, and Will Briscoe) – 0
Payouts
Payouts will be sent once all league fees are confirmed.
1st Place: You’re My Boy Blue! – $250
2nd Place: DolFan Madness – $75
3rd Place: Finding Nico – $25
Best Regular Season Record: DolFan Madness, King Will & You’re My Boy Blue – $50 each = $150
Most Regular Season Points: DolFan Madness – $100
If you still owe league fees, Venmo me ASAP (@mdmuchnick). I’ll reconcile payouts once everything is settled.  People I show as still owing me are Jack Muchnick, Jeff Ready, Greg Stiefvater, and Andrew Briscoe.
Looking Ahead
Keeper rules will remain unchanged. Two keepers per team, 1st round pick for keeping someone for multiple seasons.   Let me know if we should consider a cap on the years a player can be kept.   I’m going to officially make the call that next year’s draft order will be a reverse of this year’s playoff standings finish.   Since I ended up first, I think that’s fair to do.    Would also entertain the idea of a guillotine league too.   I hear that’s a lot of fun.
Please let me know if you’re not planning to return next season, though after 24 years, I’m optimistic we’ll keep the streak alive.
Thanks again to everyone for another competitive, entertaining season. Same league, same chaos, and hopefully the same group back again next year.
Happy New Year to you all! 
Marc

2016.text:
I'd like to congratulate John Briscoe on winning his first MFFL Championship.      While not the first team to win from the Wild Card 6 seed with a 7-6 regular season record, it has to be the first time a team won with the 4th to last total points.  This season does mark the first time no team won more than 9 games, not to mention a team with the most total points didn’t even make the playoffs - Steve Smith.   But, congrats to John, he made some good waiver moves and rode Le'veon Bell all the way to the trophy.  He was able to overcome a season ending injury to his #2 overall pick as well.    I’m sure he’s relishing in his season story which projected his draft finish to be 11th place yet ended with the MFFL Cup.

Jeff Ready ends up in 2nd place this year relinquishing his trophy in what I’m pretty sure is the first time we’ve had a finals rematch.   Jeff still takes home 2nd place prize money as well as the best regular season record at 9-4.   As stated above, congrats to Steve Smith who wins the most points prize money, despite missing the playoffs.   How you missed the playoffs with Luck, Mike Evans, TY Hilton and Ezekiel Elliott is amazing to me.   You did allow the 2nd most points on defense behind Chris’s 1543 points allowed.  The Sacko for the year goes to my brother, Loren Muchnick with a league low 1286 points.  He was never able to overcome Gronk’s injuries and the ineptitude of the Jaguars offense.   And then there’s my team with a draft projected finish of 1st place yet a  9th place  result. I blame it all on Steve King who took Derrick Carr 2 picks ahead of me in the 10th round.  My hold out sleeper QB strategy was a bust.  Congratulations to all the winners!   Payouts will come from PayPal momentarily.
